citations.quote: What broke the deal is the way you talk to him in the first seconds of the call.

diagnosis.text: The problem lies in asking the same series of questions that provide no real value or connection to clients, leading them to withdraw.

cases.title: Common Mistakes in Initial Client Calls

citations.quote: Quick example. John joined my coaching academy already closing deals, but only with people he knew personally.

situation.text: John, a participant in the coaching academy, was closing deals only with people he knew personally but struggled with new leads from social media.

citations.quote: We fixed the structure of his conversations. And just after one session, he went back to his own leads and closed two deals on the first month.

strategy.text: By fixing the structure of his conversations, John improved his control over new leads.

citations.quote: and this is exact reason you're losing deals, because after you send them even the perfect options, the client just disappears.

observation.text: The speaker starts with an illustrative scenario of a common issue, explains why it happens, and proposes a solution that challenges common assumptions.

citations.quote: there are only two types of agents. The first are people pleasers and order takers.

observation.text: The speaker contrasts people pleasers and order takers with expert agents, highlighting different approaches and their outcomes.

citations.quote: if you recognize yourself for the first category, you can shift to become an expert as well.

purpose.text: To encourage agents to shift towards being experts who lead conversations.

citations.quote: Well, I'm not saying never ask how are you. Call two, three, ask about the wife, the kids, the dog, it works there. But on a call one,
A stranger asking how are you doesn't sound like a care. It sounds like a start of the pitch. Will you get back?

summary.text: In the first call with a client, asking 'how are you?' can sound insincere and like the start of a sales pitch, putting the client on guard and making it harder to have a genuine conversation.

knowledge.title: Problem with Asking 'How are you?' in Initial Calls

you like to invest? Now the client freezes because in reality he's not maybe downtown Dubai Marina, maybe one or two more.

summary.text: Agents often start calls by assuming that the client wants to buy, leading clients to correct them or freeze due to lack of information, which can kill the deal.

summary.text: Agents should ask questions to understand the client's intent and motivations rather than making assumptions or pushing for immediate decisions.
